_about: The Bococho (src/bococho_encounter.py, src/game_race.py, src/race.py, src/underway_run.py, src/riding.py, src/game_riding.py; RARE_PETS_PLAN_2026_11_14 section 3). Every run, on one floor of 51-65 (never a gate boss's floor), a racing camp in a cavern: Gilt Varro (he), a loud, greedy race-runner, keeps his birds on short tethers and races them for bets. One young Bococho (she), faster than any of them, will not run for him, and he means to sell her to the knacker. Feed her Sunroot on two visits with time between; then challenge Varro (a fee in gold), and race his best bird, Brassbeak, on the Underway Run (a side floor, 996). Win, and she is free: 'I choose you!' asks the animal quiz, as for the Emberpup. Lose, and try again after a while, at the fee again. The Bococho is a homage, never a copy: her call is her own ('whirrup'), never the original's. Every individual is he or she.
_feed_gap_turns_note: Turns she needs between two Sunroots (and between a lost race and the next challenge, and after a failed 'I choose you!'). Leaving the camp's floor counts as waiting.
_food_id_note: The one food she takes: Sunroot, a forage find from floor 40 (data/items/ingredient.json). Any other food she sniffs at and turns from ('not_sunroot').
_race_fee_share_note: Varro's fee, as a share of one floor's income on the camp's floor (economy.share): a little under a quarter of a floor's gold, paid to him, every challenge.
_quiz_note: 'I choose you!' after the race is won: the animal quiz, as for the Emberpup (whose is tier 2, two right; she is met deeper).

camp._posts_note: Tether posts set against the camp room's wall: Varro's two birds at the first two, the young Bococho at the third.

varro_bird.name: Varro's Racing Bird
varro_bird.bump: The tethered bird shies to the end of his rope, as far from you as it will let him go. His ribs show beneath the feathers, and upon his flank are the old marks of a crop.

varro.name: Gilt Varro
varro._stats_note: A race-runner, not a warrior, but a big man of the deep Underway: about a fighting mortal of his depth (the veteran knight, the cult hierophant). He fights only when struck (his screen's third choice).
varro.lore: Gilt Varro holds races in the deep Underway, where the great running birds live wild, and no one there has ever seen him lose a wager that he set up himself. He buys birds cheap, keeps them on short ropes, feeds them little and works them hard, and all the gold he wins goes into his coat. He is loud and greedy and mean, and in all his life he has never fought anything that had the strength to fight back.
varro.kill_chronicle: Killed Gilt Varro, who starved his birds. The young Bococho and the rest fled.

story: A great cavern opens off the passage, lit by smoky lanterns that hang from tether posts. Racing birds stand at the posts, tall golden runners with crests and strong legs, each tied short by one leg and so thin that their ribs show through the feathers. A chalk board on an easel gives the odds for the day's races in a loud and crooked hand.

Apart from the rest, at a post of her own, stands a young Bococho, smaller and thinner than any of the others, and the rope on her leg is frayed where she has fought against it. As you draw near she flattens her crest and backs to the end of her tether, stamping and ready to bolt, for someone has handled her roughly and she has not forgotten it.

Beside the board a loud man in a gold-trimmed coat watches you with a riding crop in his fist. "That one won't run," he calls to you. "She has the fastest legs in the Underway and she won't run one step for me, so the knacker takes her at the end of the week."
waiting: The young Bococho backs to the end of her tether as you come near, her crest laid flat, ready to bolt, for someone has handled her roughly and she has not forgotten it.
The young Bococho watches you from her post. Though she still backs away, she stops short of the rope's end now, and her eyes are upon your pack, where the Sunroot was.
When the young Bococho sees you she lifts her crest and steps up to meet you, as far as the rope allows, and she lets you stroke it. You can tell that she trusts you and that she would run for you.
waiting_won: Though she is free of her rope, the young Bococho does not run away. She stands beside you with lowered head, and from time to time she nudges your hand, as if there were something that she wished to ask.
no_food: You hold out your hand, and she sniffs the air for something sweet and finds nothing there to her liking. The great running birds of the Underway will cross a cavern for one thing only, and that is a Sunroot.
not_sunroot: You hold out your {food}, but when she has sniffed at it she turns her head away and stamps. The great running birds of the Underway will cross a cavern for one thing only, and that is a Sunroot.
fed: You hold out the Sunroot at the length of your arm. She stretches her neck as far as the tether allows and snatches it, and then she crunches it at the end of the rope with her eyes upon you all the while. She is wary still, but she has eaten from your hand.

This time she does not back away, but takes the Sunroot gently and crunches it before your eyes, and when it is gone she lowers her head and lets you stroke her crest. Her feathers are warm, and she gives a soft, rolling whirrup, which is the first sound that you have heard from her.
fed_again: She crunches the Sunroot happily and nudges your shoulder for more, for already she trusts you.
_too_soon_note: Back before feed_gap_turns: one line per feed so far (data, like the Emberpup's), and nothing counts.
too_soon: The young Bococho is still crunching the last root, and flicks her crest at you.
The young Bococho is still crunching the last root, and though she flicks her crest at you, she does not back away now.
refused: You hold out your hand and say it, but she shies to the end of her rope and stamps, for she does not trust you yet.
refused_trust: She looks from your hand to your face and backs away a step. She is warming to you, but she needs a little more time before she can be sure.
refused_tethered: She presses her head into your hands, and then she looks beyond you to Varro and his crop. So long as she is his she can go nowhere, but if you beat his best bird she will be free to choose.
refused_soon: She is still unsure after the last time, and she pecks at the dirt rather than look at you. You had best give her a little while.
ignore: You leave the young Bococho at her post, and she watches you as you go.
pass: She lifts her head and looks at you for a long moment. Then she steps up beside you, folds her long legs and kneels, as a riding bird kneels for a rider whom she trusts, and gives a bright, proud whirrup that rings all round the cavern. The frayed end of her old rope is knotted on her leg still, and you untie it. Now she belongs to no one but herself, and of her own will she has chosen you.
fail: You say it, but the words come out wrong, and she steps aside from you in doubt. She has had a hard week, so give her a little while before you ask again.
name_prompt: Will you give your Bococho a name?
named_message: {name} the Bococho runs for you now, and for nobody else.
unnamed_message: Your Bococho runs for you now, and for nobody else.
named_chronicle: Beat Varro's bird. The young Bococho he'd have killed chose me. Named her {name}.
unnamed_chronicle: Beat Gilt Varro's bird. The young Bococho he'd have killed chose me.
varro_story: "Gilt Varro, race-runner, at your service," says the man in the gold coat, though he makes no bow. His hat has a plume as long as your arm, and betting slips stick out of his belt like feathers. "Every bird in this camp is mine, and every one of them runs when I say, all but her," he says, and he jabs the crop toward the young Bococho.

"Unless," he says, and his grin grows wider, "you think that you can make her run. Put up a fee and race her against my best bird on the Underway Run. If you beat Brassbeak the scrawny thing is yours, and if you lose, I keep the fee." And he laughs like a man who has never seen Brassbeak beaten.

varro_waiting.untrusted: Varro leans on the betting board, picking his teeth. "You would race with her? She won't run for you any more than she will for me. Get her eating out of your hand first, if you can."
varro_waiting.trusted: Varro looks from you to the young Bococho, who rests her head on your shoulder, and his grin grows thin. "Well, well, fancy that. Still, it's one thing for her to like you and quite another to beat Brassbeak." The fee is {fee} gold.
varro_waiting.lost: Varro counts your gold again, slowly, so that you can see. "Back for more, are you? It's the same fee as before, {fee} gold, and Brassbeak could use the exercise."

options_varro.challenge: Challenge him to a race ({fee} gold)

challenge_untrusted: "She won't run for you," says Varro, laughing. "Come back when she'll eat out of your hand."
challenge_soon: "Brassbeak is still blowing from the last race," says Varro, with his eyes upon his slips. "Come back later, if you've a mind to lose again."
challenge_poor: Varro looks at your purse and laughs. "That wouldn't buy Brassbeak's breakfast, and the fee is {fee} gold."
challenge_accepted: Varro takes your {fee} gold, bites one coin and tucks it away. "Done, and it's off to the Underway Run with us." He unties Brassbeak, a big bird in a harness of gold and purple, and leads the way down a long tunnel, and the young Bococho follows at your heel with no one to lead her.
leave_varro: You leave Varro to his slips, and already he is chalking new odds upon the board.
strike: You raise your weapon, and the grin falls from Varro's face. "You'd strike a man over a BIRD?" he shrieks, and he comes at you with the crop.
strike_bolts: The young Bococho screams and rears against her rope until the frayed strands part, and in three long strides she is gone into the dark of the tunnels. She has seen enough of men with sticks, and she will not trust a hero who fights in front of her.
strike_chronicle: Struck Gilt Varro in his camp. The young Bococho bolted. No race now.
varro_dies_birds: When Varro is gone, his birds pull at their ropes until the old knots give way, and one by one they slip free and run lightly off into the dark, and not one of them looks back.
won_back: Varro flings his hat in the dirt and stamps on it. "Cheat! Witch! That bird was MINE!" he cries, but no one heeds him, and he storms off down the tunnel, shouting still, and leaves his birds behind.
You cut the tethers one by one. The runners stand blinking a little while, and then they trot off into the dark, and not one of them looks back.
The young Bococho alone does not run. She stays at your side, blowing and proud, and nudges your hand.
lost_back: Back at the camp Varro tosses your fee in his hand and grins. "Better luck next time, friend, or maybe not." The young Bococho hangs her head, but you may try again in a while if you have the fee.

log.shied: The young Bococho sidesteps away, unsure.

race._doc: src/race.py. Five legs; each is one maths chain at the hero's own maths tier (the weapon in his hand, as in combat), capped at max_chain. A leg's lengths = base_per_leg + chain x stride[tier] (a harder sum is worth more ground: the stride follows the time a sum of that tier takes, so no weapon is a handicap or a trick). Sprint: x sprint_mult, costs sprint_cost wind (with less, only part of the boost: a tired sprint), and the NEXT leg runs winded (x winded_mult). Pace: wind back by pace_recover. The home straight (the last leg) gets up to final_kick more from the wind left. Leg cheat_leg: the inside lane is salted with caltrops (x caltrops_mult); the outside is clean but longer (x outside_mult). Brassbeak runs varro_pace by leg, give or take varro_luck from the race's own seed. Tuned 2026-11-14 by a simulator of kids (answer times from tools/balance/difficulty_sim.py ANSWER_SECONDS): a mastery-level kid (92% right, fast, 20 s clock) who paces well (pace to the home straight, then sprint, and takes the outside lane on leg 3) wins 81-90% of races at tiers 2-4; the same kid sprinting every leg and keeping the inside wins 3-5%; a good kid (88%, a little slower) who paces well wins about 40-46% (two tries, about); a sloppy kid (75%, slow) loses nearly every time.
race.title: THE UNDERWAY RUN
arrival: The Underway Run is a great oval scraped in the floor of a cavern, with its sand raked smooth and a wooden rail along either edge. Lanterns hang from the roof on long chains, and a banner upon two poles marks the finish.
Varro leads Brassbeak to the line, and the young Bococho walks up beside the big bird and stands there, small and thin and stubborn, while you take your place at the rail by the finish.
race.door_line: The gate back to the camp is the way out (> on it). Leaving before the finish gives Varro the race.
race.how: Every sum you get right, she hears from the rail and lengthens her stride. A Sprint goes half again as far, but she runs the next leg winded. A Pace keeps her wind for the home straight.
taunts: "Look at those legs, as thin as sticks! She'll fold before the first bend," Varro jeers from the far rail.
"Brassbeak is only warming up," Varro calls, "for he likes to give them hope first."

"Hug the inside rail on the back straight, friend," Varro calls, much too kindly, "for it's the short way round." You see a grey dust of iron on his gloves, and a little leather bag is missing from his belt.
"Still on your feet? Brassbeak, stop playing with her!" Varro shouts.
"Home straight! Brassbeak never loses a home straight!" cries Varro, who is up on the rail and waving his hat.

modes.sprint: Sprint: half again as far, then a winded leg
modes.pace: Pace: steady, and she gets her wind back

lane_line.inside: Lane: Inside, the short way round

race.winded_now: She is still blowing from the sprint: this leg runs short.

events.winded: She is blowing hard from the sprint, and her stride is short.
events.sprint: You call her on, and she sprints, head low, legs a blur.
events.tired_sprint: She tries to sprint again, but there is not much left in her legs.
events.pace: She settles into a long, steady stride.
events.kick: Her wind holds, and she has plenty left for the home straight.
events.caltrops: There are iron caltrops in the sand on the inside! She hops and stumbles through them and loses ground.
events.outside: You swing her wide, and she runs clean past a scatter of iron caltrops on the inside rail. Varro swears.

standing.lead_big: She is flying now, {gap} clear of Brassbeak!
standing.level: The two run neck and neck, and there is nothing between them!
standing.behind_big: Brassbeak is {gap} clear, and Varro is waving his hat.

race.photo: They cross the line side by side, so nearly equal that none can call it. The old judge crouches by the finish banner and squints along the line, and at last he points.
race.won_beak: Your Bococho wins by a beak!
race.won: The young Bococho crosses the line ahead and comes back to you at a trot, blowing and proud, while Varro's face turns the colour of his coat lining.
race.lost: Varro whoops and throws his hat in the air. The young Bococho hangs her head, but she comes back to you none the less.
race.forfeit: You step away from the rail, and Varro grins and calls the race for Brassbeak and pockets your fee.
race.forfeit_ask: Leave the race? Varro keeps your fee, and Brassbeak wins.
race.won_chronicle: Won on the Underway Run. The young Bococho beat Varro's Brassbeak.
race.lost_chronicle: Lost on the Underway Run, and my fee to Varro. Must race him again.

pet._start_level_note: She is a young runner who has just beaten the best bird in the Underway, grown enough to race and to carry a rider: she starts as a Bococho (stage 1, level 25: LORE NOT FLOOR, her own story, never the floor). The Chick is her line's first stage; no sphere hatches one.
pet._saddlebags_note: While she is out with the hero (alive, on his floor, not in her sphere), her saddlebags carry this much: Player.get_carry_limit adds it, so the Light, Heavy, Burdened and Overloaded lines all move up with it (Player.saddlebag_lb, kept by Game._sync_saddlebags).

species._bite_mult_note: Strong kicks: a quarter harder than the growth table's bite at her level (data/pet_growth.json is everyone's).

riding._doc: src/riding.py, src/game_riding.py. Mounted, each step covers two tiles: the second only if the first was clear and the second is walkable, and both tiles trigger traps and hazards. One move is one turn for the monsters (no free turns). She is under the hero: not drawn apart, and she does not act. Set down at once, with a line, by a hostile coming into view, a blow, a trap or hazard, any quiz starting, the stairs (she follows), a status that unseats, being Overloaded, or her being stored or hurt.
riding._min_stage_note: The chick is too small to carry a rider; she joins as a grown Bococho (pet.start_level).
riding._step_noise_note: Tiles added to the hero's footsteps (senses.step_radius) while he rides: a galloping bird is loud.
riding._sleeper_note: How much readier the deep sleepers of a zoo, graveyard or barracks are to stir at her running feet (sleepers.factor 'step').
riding._seat_note: Where the rider's hips sit in each saddled picture's 64 px frame (x, y): the art run's own measure (tools/content/genart/install_rare_pets.py SEAT, a hero at about 0.6 scale with his hips there).
